newsitem.title: BERMUDA: UK's Clarke hopes for early debt relief agreement.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke hopes for early debt relief agreement.

text.p: Wealthy countries are determined to resolve the issue of debt relief for the poorest countries but are unlikely to agree on the details, such as gold sales, at next week's annual IMF/World Bank meeting, UK Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Thursday.

There is still opposition from some countries, notably Germany, to selling International Monetary Fund gold to bridge a gap in setting up a system to help the world's poorest countries shake off their crippling debt burden.

"Everyone is committed to resolving this issue if we possibly can at next week's meeting. There is no one arguing against the need to produce a result of this kind. I hope the preparatory work has got us all near enough to come to a satisfactory solution next week," Clarke told reporters.
Clarke proposed the gold sales as a means to bridge a gap in financing a bailout of poor debtor countries.

"What we need next week is an agreement that finance will be forthcoming to bridge this gap...I am not expecting that we will get down to details of...how much gold will be sold and when," he said at the end of a Commonwleath finance ministers meeting in Bermuda.
Clarke said Britain, the U.S. and Canada would all press for agreement next week on the need to get help to the poor, an issue that dominated the Commonwealth meeting here.
"Don't expect the gold sales to be signed up (next week)," a British official said.
